card.name: Prepositions before cell or body locations
card.fires_on: Small location words (in, on, from, of, outside) or verbs like inhabit that come right before a cell, organelle or chromosome location in biology text. The next word is likely a cell part or body site.

modes.label: Location preposition
modes.description: A preposition after found, located, or emanating that points to a cell type or chromosome arm.
modes.example: The ROR2 gene is located<< on>> the long (q) arm of chromosome

modes.label: Microbe and cell setting
modes.description: A word placing a microbe relative to a host cell or gut.
modes.example: 00 strain of Staphylococcus aureus bacteria, colorized in gold, shown<< outside>> a white blood cell.

card.writes: It nudges the output toward biology words like pathogens and wound, though the effect is weak.
card.plain: It fires on little place words in cell biology text, just before the cell or body part where something is found.
